To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the two tests we developed are very powerful in detecting recent bottlenecks; 2) the bottleneck can be detected even if the bottleneck was very short (a few generations); 3) the bottleneck can also be detected if the time since the beginning of bottleneck is very long (several hundred generations); 4) the two tests are very sensitive to the level of variability of markers; 5) the two tests can be used with a wide range of sample sizes;

the tests are most useful for detecting recent bottlenecks, that they can be applied to a wide range of species, that the tests are best applied to loci evolving according to the infinite allele model and finally, the tests are best used when sample sizes are large.
the two tests are powerful and robust for detecting recent population size changes.
